title: Add alerts for max-bound saturation and sustained queue buildup (Dedicated autoscaling bounds)
creator: Allison Grant
project: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
content:
Context
Dedicated autoscaling bounds adds hard min/max clamps to desired capacity. When a deployment is capped at its max, reactive/predictive scaling can continue to “want” more replicas, but the bounded desired cannot increase. Without explicit alerting, we can miss the early signal that the customer is saturating their contractual ceiling and will start queueing / violating latency SLOs.

This ticket defines and ships alert thresholds, paging routing, and runbook integration for:
1) sustained MAX bound saturation
2) sustained queue buildup (especially when MAX bound is binding)

Related docs / artifacts
- Confluence: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/dedicated-autoscaling-slo-and-alerting-updates.json
- Confluence: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/autoscaling-bounds-observability-dashboard-spec.json
- Confluence: sources/confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/dedicated-autoscaler-troubleshooting-runbook.json
- Observability standards: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/metric-naming-for-scaling-and-capacity.json
- Implementation metrics/logs: (paired with ENG-22143) sources/github/redwood/pr-48241-add-metrics-desired-vs-bounded-capacity.json
- Alerts PR: sources/github/observability-pack/pr-1941-add-alert-rules-max-bound-saturation.json

Goal
Page the right team when a Dedicated deployment is at max bound and customer-facing queueing/latency risk is sustained, while minimizing alert noise during expected short spikes.

Non-goals
- Alerts for MIN bound unmet during region shortage (tracked separately under ENG-22151).
- Automated customer comms; we only provide the on-call signal + runbook steps.

Signals / metrics used (per observability standards)
(Exact metric names come from ENG-22143 / PR-48241; alert rules match those names.)
- Bounded capacity indicators:
  - redwood_dedicated_autoscaler_unbounded_desired_replicas{deployment_id,region}
  - redwood_dedicated_autoscaler_bounded_desired_replicas{deployment_id,region}
  - redwood_dedicated_autoscaler_bound_hit_total{deployment_id,region,bound="max"}
  - redwood_dedicated_autoscaler_decision_total{deployment_id,region}
- Queue / latency indicators:
  - redwood_dedicated_queue_depth{deployment_id,region}
  - redwood_dedicated_queue_wait_ms_bucket{deployment_id,region} (for p95/p99)
  - redwood_dedicated_request_latency_ms_bucket{deployment_id,region} (optional cross-check)

Alerting design
We ship two primary alerts, each with warning + critical severities.

A) DedicatedMaxBoundSaturation
Intent: detect when the autoscaler is repeatedly requesting > max and is clamped at max for a sustained interval.

Derived expression
- bound_hit_rate = rate(redwood_dedicated_autoscaler_bound_hit_total{bound="max"}[10m])
- decision_rate = rate(redwood_dedicated_autoscaler_decision_total[10m])
- bound_hit_ratio = bound_hit_rate / clamp_min(decision_rate, 1e-6)

Warning (non-paging)
- Condition: bound_hit_ratio > 0.20 for 15m
- AND unbounded_desired > bounded_desired (to avoid false positives when metrics jitter)
- Action: notify #eng-dedicated-observability (Slack), create incident card (no page)

Critical (paging)
- Condition: bound_hit_ratio > 0.60 for 10m
- AND unbounded_desired >= bounded_desired + 1
- AND bounded_desired_replicas >= 1 (avoid edge cases; scale-to-zero prevented elsewhere)
- Routing: Dedicated on-call (SRE rotation) + #incidents-dedicated

Rationale
- 10–15m windows reduce noise from brief bursts.
- Using the ratio avoids page storms on deployments with very frequent decision loops.

B) DedicatedQueueBuildupAtMaxBound
Intent: page only when max-bound saturation is associated with user-visible queueing risk.

Warning (non-paging)
- Condition (any of the following, sustained 10m):
  - queue_depth > 0 for 10m AND queue_wait_p95_ms > 250ms
- AND max-bound is binding (unbounded_desired > bounded_desired OR bound_hit_ratio > 0.20)
- Routing: #eng-dedicated-observability (Slack)

Critical (paging)
- Condition (sustained 10m):
  - queue_wait_p95_ms > 2000ms OR queue_depth is persistently increasing (slope > 0 over 10m)
- AND max-bound is binding (bound_hit_ratio > 0.60)
- Routing: Dedicated on-call (SRE rotation) + #incidents-dedicated

Rationale
- This is the customer-impacting alert. It intentionally requires BOTH: queueing + evidence we’re capped.
- p95 wait is used rather than instantaneous depth to better align with user-visible pain.

Cardinality / scope controls
- Alerts are grouped by (deployment_id, region). We explicitly do NOT group by customer_id to avoid accidental cardinality blowups.
- The alert annotation includes deployment_id and a Console deep link to the per-deployment dashboard (dashboard resolves account/customer context).
- During Pilot, alerts are enabled only for deployments with the autoscaling-bounds feature flag enabled (per-account/deployment gating). Post-GA we keep them global for Dedicated, but we retain silencing guidance in the runbook.

Paging + escalation policy
- Warning notifications: Slack only (#eng-dedicated-observability).
- Critical notifications: PagerDuty service “Dedicated SRE / Capacity” (the same service used for Dedicated latency/SLO pages) + Slack #incidents-dedicated.
- If the alert fires during a known planned event and customer-approved, on-call may silence for up to 2 hours with a linked ticket and customer confirmation.

Runbook integration requirements
Update runbook (owner: Rafael Mendes) to include an explicit “MAX bound saturation / queue buildup” section:
- How to confirm bound-hit state (dashboard panels: unbounded vs bounded desired, bound_hit_ratio)
- How to validate it’s not a predictor bug (if predictive mode enabled): check prediction freshness + staleness counters
- Immediate mitigations (in order):
  1) Confirm if customer-set max is intended (check scaling policy + recent audit events)
  2) If customer approves: raise max bound temporarily (or request CS/TAM approval depending on account)
  3) If customer does NOT approve: enable graceful degradation via routing policy (fallback model/region if permitted) without exceeding bounds
  4) If there is evidence of platform regression (queueing at low utilization): engage Fleet autoscaling (Vanessa/Keiko) and Runtime signals (eng-runtime)
- Escalation path: if sustained >30m and customer is violating SLA, open incident and loop PM (Lauren Bishop) + TAM.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Alert rules merged to observability-pack and deployed to canary region first.
- [x] Warning/critical severity definitions reviewed by SRE (Rafael) and Observability (Allison).
- [x] Paging routes to correct PD service; verified via test firing in staging.
- [x] Alert annotations include runbook link and dashboard link.
- [x] Alert noise evaluated during pilot week; thresholds adjusted once based on real data.
- [x] Runbook updated with a dedicated section and mitigations.

Testing / validation plan
- Staging: set a test Dedicated deployment max=2 replicas; replay a ramp load until unbounded_desired requests >2.
- Confirm:
  - DedicatedMaxBoundSaturation warning fires ~15m, critical fires ~10m if sustained.
  - DedicatedQueueBuildupAtMaxBound critical only fires when queue_wait_p95_ms exceeds threshold.
- Production canary: enable for 1 pilot account in us-east-1 for 48 hours; monitor false positive rate and page volume.

Implementation notes
- Implemented in sources/github/observability-pack/pr-1941-add-alert-rules-max-bound-saturation.json
- Alert naming follows existing Redwood conventions: Dedicated<Signal><Condition>.
- All annotations include:
  - deployment_id
  - region
  - runbook URL (Confluence)
  - dashboard URL (Grafana panel + variables)

Updates / comments

2025-07-09 (Rafael Mendes)

2025-07-23 (Sergio Costa)
- Tuned queue_wait critical from 1s -> 2s after pilot incident review to avoid paging on short ramps that self-resolve within cooldown windows.

2025-07-29 (Allison Grant)
- Deployed alert rules to canary and expanded to pilot deployments. Marking done; follow-ups tracked in PM-1842 retro items.

Follow-ups (not blocking)
- Consider adding an informational alert for “NearMaxBound” (e.g., bounded_desired == max for 30m even without queueing) to support proactive CS outreach (would be Slack-only).
- Evaluate adding a burn-rate style SLO alert keyed off queue_wait_p99 to better match customer experience for bursty workloads.
